s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic hematochezia in an immunocompromised patient with gastrointestinal polyps and mixed inflammatory infiltrate
salient_findings: Multiple semisessile polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon
Mixed inflammatory infiltrate with pale histiocytes and eosinophils
Basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes
key_facts: 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
Receiving maintenance therapy with 6-mercaptopurine, methotrexate, vincristine, and dexamethasone
Intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
Denies abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
Stool studies negative for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus
Colonoscopy showed multiple polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon
Histologic examination revealed eroded surface mucosa and reactive hyperplastic glands
Lamina propria expanded by dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate
Histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions
Inclusions were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains
Fungal and acid-fast stains were negative for organisms
